Use the supplied first and last frames as exact composition anchors for one continuous transition.

The scene is the same physical worktable: a pale ash desk border, one warm ivory graph-paper sheet, twelve matte paper cards with abstract charcoal marks, soft indigo contact shadows, restrained Chordnote-violet guide marks, a high slightly oblique top-down camera, and upper-left light. Keep the desk, paper grain, grid scale, card identities, colors, empty upper-left copy space, ground contact, and shadows identical across the entire shot. The background is part of the final picture: no chroma key, flat backdrop, background replacement, or transparency.

Locked camera and locked framing. No pan, tilt, zoom, orbit, shake, reframing, perspective change, lens change, or lighting change. Preserve the same twelve cards, desk, paper, scale, material, silhouette, and identity in all frames. No people, hands, faces, devices, readable text, logos, UI, watermarks, borders, neon, glossy CGI, or new objects.

Create one smooth, physically plausible tabletop action from K0 to K1. The twelve scattered paper cards slide and rotate gently along the existing graphite grid, settling into three measured study clusters with even spacing and a clear central passage. Existing short violet guide marks stay attached to their paper groups and become slightly more legible as the clusters settle; do not draw long cross-cluster links yet. Every intermediate frame must read clearly when playback stops. No cuts, dissolves, jump movement, sudden speed changes, or pauses. Arrive exactly at the supplied last-frame arrangement.
